captions.detailed: An Alpine wooden bell cote featuring a narrow, dark brown rectangular timber frame and a pointed, gabled dark roof. Inside the frame, a single brass-colored bell with a flared rim hangs from a dark horizontal pivot beam. The bell is mounted via a revolute joint, allowing it to swing freely back and forth about the horizontal axis of the headstock.
captions.instruction: Generate an Alpine wooden bell cote with a dark brown rectangular timber frame, a pointed gabled roof, and a brass-colored bell. The bell should be mounted to a horizontal pivot beam inside the frame with a revolute joint so it can swing about the horizontal axis.
captions.factory: Construct the main frame using box primitives for the vertical posts, horizontal crossbeams, and a bottom base. Create the gabled roof by combining two angled box plates joined at the ridge. Model the bell using a revolved profile or a series of lofted/conical shapes, and attach it to a central horizontal cylinder pivot. Define a revolute joint between the stationary timber frame (parent) and the bell/pivot assembly (child) with the rotation axis aligned horizontally.
